title: Bounce Cause and the Customer's Share of a Mobile Wallet Resend Charge
content:
Training notes on **Mobile Wallet** resend charges: what share of the charge the customer bears depends on why the credit last bounced.

**Rule.** The cause of the latest bounce on the transfer, that is the rejection reason on its most recent reversed-credit entry, sets the share of the resend charge the customer bears:

| Rejection reason on the latest reversed credit | Side | Share of the resend charge the customer bears |
|---|---|---|
| provider unavailable | Paloma's or the provider's side | none (0) |
| wallet limit exceeded | recipient's side | 0.80 (80 percent) |
| wallet suspended | recipient's side | 0.80 (80 percent) |
| wallet not registered, wallet name mismatch, wallet number invalid, or any other recipient-side cause | recipient's side | the whole charge (1) |

### Questions the rule answers
**Which bounce counts when a transfer has bounced more than once?** Only the latest: the most recent reversed-credit entry on the transfer.

**Does an earlier provider-unavailable bounce matter if the latest one was a wallet-limit rejection?** No. The latest cause is wallet limit exceeded, so the customer bears 0.80 of the charge.

**What does the customer bear when the latest bounce was provider unavailable?** None of the charge.

*Hypothetical figure:* on a charge figure of 2.50, a latest bounce of wallet suspended leaves the customer bearing 0.80 of it, that is 2.00; a latest bounce of wallet number invalid leaves the whole 2.50.
